paragraphs: R' Shimon son of R' Yishmael.

He is mentioned in Shemot Rabbah, where he said: “It is a testimony to all who come into the world that there is forgiveness for Israel.” The saying is also cited in [Tanchuma, Pekudei 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma_Buber,_Pekudei.2.1), where it reads: “R' Yishmael said.” Buber conjectures there that someone noted beside it the variant reading “R' Shimon”; a second person then combined the two readings, producing “R' Shimon son of Yishmael.”[^1]

notes.text: The Shemot Rabbah locator is printed ש״ר פג״א-ד. The earlier translation’s “chapter 43, sections 1–4” was unsupported and is withdrawn; the exact compressed locator remains unresolved. Tanchuma is printed פקודי-ב. Buber is introduced as הר״ש בובער; his personal initial is not expanded. The final combined form is printed ר״ש ב״י, rendered from the heading and the two expressly named variants in Hyman’s explanation. שאחר means another person, not a later scribe; בצדו means beside it, without specifying a margin. Buber’s conjecture is Hyman’s attributed report, not independently verified textual history.

The checked Buber edition of Tanchuma, Pekudei 2, gives the saying in the name of ר׳ ישמעאל. It does not spell out the title; R' is therefore retained in this translation. The standard Tanchuma passage at the same section number is different, so the link points to Buber’s recension. Buber’s conjecture about the combined readings remains Hyman’s report; the cited Shemot Rabbah locator and the editorial history have not been independently established.
